INTRODUCTION TO THE APOCRYPHON OF YEHOSHUA

1 The Apocryphon of Yehoshua is a Hebrew composition from the Qumran Cave 4 corpus presenting additional psalms, speeches, and episodes attributed to Yehoshua bin Nun, leader of Yisra'el after Moshe. The text supplements and in some places preserves earlier traditions than those found in the Masoretic Sefer Yehoshua.

2 The composition includes a psalm of Yehoshua at the Jordan crossing, a speech concerning covenant renewal at Shechem, a prayer before the conquest, and a striking prophetic passage concerning a false prophet who will arise. These traditions were known to the Qumran community as authentic Yehoshua material.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q378 and 4Q379 were published by Carol Newsom in the DJD series. The manuscripts date to the Herodian period though the composition itself is considerably older. The text demonstrates that the Qumran community possessed Yehoshua traditions not preserved in the Masoretic canon.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez canon contains the Masoretic Yehoshua without significant variation. However the theological framework of the Apocryphon — covenant renewal, the centrality of YHWH's direct guidance, the danger of false prophets — is entirely consistent with the Ge'ez theological tradition.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Sefer Yehoshua preserves the narrative of the conquest and settlement. The Apocryphon of Yehoshua preserves the psalmic and prophetic voice of Yehoshua himself — his direct address to YHWH and to Yisra'el — that the Masoretic narrative largely omits.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The existence of a Yehoshua apocryphon at Qumran confirms that the Masoretic canon does not preserve all the Yehoshua traditions that circulated in ancient Yisra'el. This is consistent with the evidence from all the other Qumran apocryphal compositions: the Masoretic canon represents a selection from a much broader ancient textual tradition.

THE APOCRYPHON OF YEHOSHUA — TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — PSALM OF YEHOSHUA AT THE YARDEN — 4Q378 Fragment 3

1 And Yehoshua spoke before YHWH saying: Blessed are You, YHWH, the God of Yisra'el, who brought us out from the house of slavery and delivered us through great signs and mighty deeds. You dried up the sea before our fathers and now You have dried up this Yarden before us.

2 You are the same YHWH who spoke to Avraham our father and swore to him by Your own name that You would give this land to his seed. This day Your word is fulfilled. This day we enter the land of promise.

3 Let all the peoples of the earth know that the hand of YHWH is mighty. Let all who fear Him take courage. For He fights for His people and no weapon formed against them shall prosper when they walk in His covenant.

4 Remember Your covenant, YHWH, with Avraham and with Yitzhak and with Yaakov. Remember the oath You swore and the word You spoke. We are the children of those fathers and we stand today in the fulfilment of Your ancient promise.

5 Guard us in the days of conquest that are coming. Let not fear enter our hearts and let not the nations overwhelm us. For You are our shield and our strength and the battle belongs to You, not to us.

6 And all Yisra'el said: Amen. And the priests lifted the ark and carried it into the midst of the Yarden and the waters stopped and the people crossed on dry ground and not one of them was lost.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q378 Fragment 3 preserves a psalm attributed to Yehoshua at the Jordan crossing. This psalm has no parallel in the Masoretic Sefer Yehoshua. The crossing narrative in Yehoshua 3-4 is purely narrative; this psalm gives voice to Yehoshua's theology at the moment of fulfilment.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The invocation of the Avrahamic covenant at the moment of entering the land parallels the Yovelim framework in the Orit Ge'ez where the covenant with Avraham is the theological foundation for all subsequent history. The land promise is not incidental but structurally central to the covenantal narrative.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Sefer Yehoshua 3-4 narrates the Jordan crossing without any psalm by Yehoshua. The Apocryphon fills this gap with psalmody consistent with the prayer tradition of the broader corpus. Whether the psalm was suppressed from the Masoretic canon or developed independently in the Qumran tradition cannot be determined from the fragments alone.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The phrase "the battle belongs to YHWH, not to us" encodes a theology of divine warfare that directly contradicts the Roman military theology of the period. Rome's conquest was legitimized by the favour of the gods, manifest in military success. The Apocryphon's theology inverts this: military outcome is determined by covenant faithfulness, not by human military strength. This is implicitly anti-imperial.

FRAGMENT 2 — THE FALSE PROPHET — 4Q379 Fragment 22

1 [And Yehoshua warned the people saying:] After I am gathered to my fathers, a man will arise among you who will speak in the name of YHWH but whose heart is not with YHWH. He will say: Thus says YHWH, but YHWH has not sent him.

2 You will know him by this sign: the thing he says in the name of YHWH will not come to pass. Or he will say: go after other gods — gods you have not known. Do not listen to the words of that prophet. Do not fear him.

3 He will perform signs that astonish and wonders that impress. But signs and wonders are not the proof of truth. The proof of truth is faithfulness to the covenant of YHWH and to all that He commanded through Moshe His servant.

4 Guard yourselves against the one who says smooth things and tells you what you wish to hear. The true prophet speaks the word of YHWH even when it is hard. The false prophet speaks the word of his own heart because it profits him.

5 In every generation there will be those who speak in YHWH's name without His authority. Test every word against the Torah and the covenant. If it does not agree with what YHWH commanded at Sinai, do not receive it, no matter who speaks it.

6 And Yehoshua said these things to all the congregation of Yisra'el and they heard and they wept. And he blessed them and sent them to their tribal portions. And he returned to his place and YHWH was with him all the days of his life.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q379 Fragment 22 contains the false prophet warning attributed to Yehoshua. This passage is remarkable for its sophisticated epistemology of prophetic testing: not signs and wonders but Torah-consistency is the criterion of true prophecy. This is a more developed prophetic epistemology than anything in the Masoretic Yehoshua.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez tradition in the Chanokh corpus warns extensively against those who lead the righteous astray with false teaching. The Apocryphon's warning from Yehoshua represents the same concern for community protection against false authority operating in the historical narrative tradition rather than the apocalyptic tradition.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Devarim 18:20-22 contains the criteria for false prophecy: the prophet whose word does not come to pass is false. The Apocryphon adds a second criterion: the prophet who leads toward other gods is false even if his words do come to pass. This is a more sophisticated prophetic epistemology that the Masoretic text contains only in fragmented form.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The criterion that signs and wonders are not proof of truth is one of the most intellectually significant statements in the entire Qumran corpus. It directly challenges both the ancient Israelite and the later Jewish and Christian traditions in which miraculous signs validate prophetic authority. The Apocryphon's epistemology is covenant-centred rather than sign-centred: Torah-consistency, not miracle-performance, determines authentic prophetic authority.
